```text
# #2962: CI: daily super run failed
Opened by @github-actions[bot].

[super run 41713495619](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41713495619) on `main` (`1b9b410`, workflow_dispatch) failed:

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| [e2e component (chrome)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41713495619/job/126192967915) | failure |

Each link opens that job's log. This issue stays open while the run is red and the next run that passes every job closes it. `gh workflow run super.yml --ref <branch>` runs it again on demand.

Night bot: this run is on `main`, so it is yours, and it comes first (`priority:high`): production promotes itself only from a run on `main` that passes every job, so it waits on this fix. Root-cause each failed job from its log and fix it in a pull request: a flake is not a root cause, so make a flaky test robust instead of re-running it, and never skip, disable or quarantine a test to get green. Reproduce it with the job's own command (CLAUDE.md, Commands; one fuzz seed is `cargo jackioh fuzz --from <seed> --seeds 1`, with `--handicap` for the handicapped wave and `--duos` for the Duos wave; a daily test is `cargo test -p <crate> <name> -- --ignored`). A pull request's CI runs only the e2e smoke specs and leaves the tests marked `#[ignore = "daily: …"]` out, so say in the pull request which job here the fix makes pass and how you checked it. You cannot change `.github/`: make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere, and when the rest needs a workflow or an action, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them.

---
_Posted by `.github/workflows/super.yml`._

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41720106523)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Make the daily super run's `e2e component (chrome)` job pass again on `main`, and keep it passing. Done means the component suite runs on the same Chrome the pinned e2e shards run on, the one failed job's root cause is fixed in this repo (not re-run, not skipped), and the pull request names that job and how it was checked. No game rule changes, so no ruling and no spec edit.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/cypress.config.ts` | change | Component block's `setupNodeEvents(on)` becomes `async setupNodeEvents(on, config)`, applies `pinChrome`, returns `config` — mirror of the e2e block |
| `e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts` | change | Header comment only: "the e2e run" becomes the Cypress run (e2e and component); constants `BROKEN_CHROME_MAJORS`, `PINNED_CHROME_MILESTONE`, `pinChrome` unchanged |
| `e2e/cypress/component/<failing>.cy.tsx` plus its source under `apps/web/src/` | change only if the pinned reproduce still fails | Robust assertion or layout fix in the one failing spec, following the patterns named in step 4 |

Do not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; no crate under `crates/`; no `retries` value, no skip/quarantine, no coverage floor. Spec sections governing this change: none (test infrastructure, not a game rule); background is `super.yml`'s `component` job comment (BUILD M5-T1 10-unit/10-backrow fixture board) and `e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts`.

## Steps

1. Reproduce with the job's own commands, on this branch: `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`, then `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome`. Note the failing spec name and its error lines; also run `google-chrome --version` and note the major.
2. Confirm the Chrome-major hypothesis from the output: the crash is the pinned one when the log shows `DevTools: Duplicate request ID`, `Network service crashed or was terminated`, requests or the Vite dev-server fetch failing mid-spec, or a whole-spec browser disconnect on Chrome 155. The e2e shards passed because only the e2e block pins (config lines 58–63); the component block (line 161) does not.
3. In `e2e/cypress.config.ts`, copy the e2e pattern into the component block: change `setupNodeEvents(on) {` to `async setupNodeEvents(on, config) {`, insert `config.browsers = await pinChrome(config.browsers, resolve(config.projectRoot, ".."));` after the `on("task", …)` registration (keeping `layout:report` as is), and `return config;` at the end. `pinChrome` and `resolve` are already imported at the top of the file. In `e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts`, update only the two header-comment spots that say "the e2e run" to say the Cypress run, e2e and component.
4. Re-run the full command from step 1. If every spec passes, stop here. If one spec still fails, fix that spec robustly, never by skipping: put the assertion inside a retrying `cy.get(…).should(…)` (the `board-layout.cy.tsx` `cy.document().should(...)` shape from #2952), name every number as a file-local `const` (`SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `PIXEL_DELTA_MIN`, `SAMPLE_STEP_PX`, following `card-versions.cy.tsx`), and for pixel sampling keep faces clear of Chrome's 256px raster-tile seams with the `FACE_GAP_PX` / `RASTER_TILE_PX` column-gap expression from `full-art-finishes.cy.tsx`. If the measurement shows a real overflow, fix the CSS under `apps/web/src/` (the #2952 `board.css` `.match-bar .clock` one-line fix is the pattern) rather than loosening the spec.
5. Run the checks in **Tests**, then `cargo jackioh patches check` only if a catalog-affecting file changed (it should not have).

## Tests

- `pnpm --dir e2e exec tsc -p cypress/component/tsconfig.json` — the component specs' own typecheck; must pass.
- `pnpm exec eslint e2e/cypress.config.ts e2e/support/chrome-pin.ts` — lint on the two edited files; must pass.
- `pnpm --dir e2e exec cypress run --component --browser chrome` — the failed job's own command (after `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh`); every spec must pass, `retries` untouched at `{ runMode: 0, openMode: 0 }`.
- If step 4 touched a web source file, also run that area's vitest file, e.g. `pnpm --dir apps/web test <file>`, naming the file in the pull request.

## Done when

- The component suite passes with the job's own command on this branch.
- `typecheck:component` and eslint on the edited files pass; `cargo fmt --check` clean (no Rust touched, nothing to reformat).
- No test skipped, disabled, quarantined, or given retries; no new `allow`, `eslint-disable`, or timeout raise.
- The pull request says the fix makes `e2e component (chrome)` pass and how it was checked (pinned reproduce command and result).
- No ruling note added (no rules decision), and `cargo jackioh spec check` still passes untouched.

## Risks

- Same Cypress interception, different path: component testing serves Vite modules rather than the preview client plus sockets, so if the failure signature is not the network-service crash, the pin helps nothing and the spec-robust fix is the real one — the reproduce step tells them apart, and the plan does the pin first because it is the only in-code gap matching the observed symptom (pinned shards green, unpinned job red).
- Pixel specs (`card-versions`, `full-art-finishes`, `animated-art`) compare rasterized output, which varies by Chrome major and GPU; thresholds must stay named constants with the tile-seam guard rather than magic numbers, or the next runner-image bump re-breaks them.
- `pinChrome` downloads Chrome for Testing into `.cache/` on CI; a failed download keeps system Chrome with a warning, so a still-red run after this fix points at that warning line, not at the specs.

## Open questions

None for a person. If a workflow or runner-image change is ever needed (e.g. removing 155 from `BROKEN_CHROME_MAJORS` once the images ship 156 everywhere), that edit lives under `.github/` or in the runner image, which the bot may not change: the builder gives the exact lines in the pull request and asks a person to make them, but this plan needs no such change now.
<!-- /jackioh-bot:plan -->
```
